articles.title: Icelanders must remain alert to possible Russian operations here
articles.description: Foreign Minister Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir says Russian attempts to recruit Danish men to assassinate a Ukrainian rapper reflect a serious security threat. Restrictions on visas for Russian nationals are among the measures being considered. Danish police announced this weekend that two Danish men were in custody on suspicion of plotting to murder a Ukrainian rapper who was planning to perform in Denmark. Russian intelligence services are suspected of having recruited the men to carry out the killing. They were arrested shortly before the concert and deny the allegations. Denmark's Ministry of Foreign Affairs intends to expel a Russian diplomat over the incident. Þorgerður Katrín Gunnarsdóttir, utanríkisráðherra (Minister for Foreign Affairs), condemned Russia's involvement in the plot in a post on social media platform X (formerly Twitter), describing reports of the assassination attempt as disturbing. I think it's important to emphasise that this reflects a very serious and deteriorating security situation. One aspect of this development is an increasing number of acts of sabotage. We're seeing cyberattacks, subversion, and both direct and indirect operations linked to the Russian authorities. Threats must be taken seriously Russia's objective is to weaken unity among European countries and their support for Ukraine. They're creating fear and undermining solidarity. Þorgerður says it is encouraging to see that these operations have had the opposite effect on allied nations, bringing them closer together. She says Icelandic authorities are examining every possible way of limiting Russia's ability to exert influence. "Here in Iceland, we've been strengthening cybersecurity. We've reinforced CERT-IS and we're strengthening cooperation, particularly the capabilities that are important for responding to the threats we now face." Þorgerður says the government is considering whether to introduce restrictions on visas for Russian nationals or other similar measures. This would be done in cooperation with the Nordic countries and Iceland's principal allies. "We're looking into this, of course in cooperation and collaboration with our main allies, and naturally we're looking first and foremost to the Nordic countries. I sense from all my counterparts that this must be taken very seriously and dealt with firmly." She says it is important to take these threats seriously. At the very least, we need to take these threats seriously. Russian influence here in Iceland is both direct and indirect, and we need to remain vigilant, just like everyone else.
